## Visulize the cloze

```{r all models}
# plot
set.seed(123)  # reproducible jitter

ggplot(highest_cloze_all, aes(x = Itemtype, y = cloze_probability)) +
  geom_violin(
    aes(fill = Itemtype),
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = Itemtype),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08),
    size = 2.2,
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    color = "red",
    size = 4,
    shape = 19
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "crossbar",
    width = 0.5,
    fatten = 3,
    color = "red"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ participant) +          # seperate screen by participant
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "English"    = "#3B6FB6",
    "CodeSwitch" = "#D97A00"
  )) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "English"    = "#3B6FB6",
    "CodeSwitch" = "#D97A00"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Highest cloze probability per item",
    x     = "Language condition",
    y     = "Max cloze Probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

```{r calculate Wasserstein distance}
# define a function
wasserstein_distance <- function(x, y) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  y <- y[!is.na(y)]
  if (length(x) == 0 || length(y) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  transport::wasserstein1d(x, y, p = 1)
}
# extract human's cloze probability
human_data <- highest_cloze_human_gpt %>%
  filter(participant == "human")
# 
gpt_data <- highest_cloze_human_gpt %>%
  filter(participant != "human")

wasserstein_results <- gpt_data %>%
  group_by(participant, Itemtype) %>%
  summarise(
    wasserstein_distance = wasserstein_distance(
      cloze_probability, # this line equals to pull(cloze_probability), to get the entire distributions instead of a mean
      human_data$cloze_probability[ 
        human_data$Itemtype == first(Itemtype) # extract the Itemtype-matched cloze_probability in human and in GPT
      ]
    ),
    .groups = "drop" # equals to ungroup()
  )

print(wasserstein_results)


# Set the order of time points
wasserstein_results <- wasserstein_results %>%
  mutate(
    participant = factor(participant, levels = c("gpt_t0", "gpt_t2", "gpt_t4", "gpt_t6", "gpt_t8", "gpt_t10", "gpt_t12", "gpt_t14")),
    Itemtype = factor(Itemtype, levels = c("English", "code_switching"), labels = c("English", "Code-switching"))
  )

# Plot
ggplot(wasserstein_results, aes(x = participant, y = wasserstein_distance, group = Itemtype, color = Itemtype)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("English" = "#3B6FB6","Code-switching" = "#D97A00")) +
  labs(
    title = "Wasserstein Distance from Human Distribution",
    x = "GPT Temperature",
    y = "Wasserstein Distance",
    color = "Language Condition"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("gpt_t0" = "0.0", "gpt_t2" = "0.2", "gpt_t4" = "0.4", "gpt_t6" = "0.6", "gpt_t8" = "0.8", "gpt_t10" = "1.0", "gpt_t12" = "1.2", "gpt_t14" = "1.4")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),legend.position = "bottom")

```

```{r}
# calculate KL-divergence
calculate_KL <- function(human, gpt) {

  human <- human[is.finite(human)]
  gpt <- gpt[is.finite(gpt)]

  if (length(human) < 2 || length(gpt) < 2) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  # Common evaluation grid
  x_grid <- seq(
    min(c(human, gpt)),
    max(c(human, gpt)),
    length.out = 2048
  )

  # Estimate density
  p <- density(human, from = min(x_grid),
               to = max(x_grid), n = 2048)

  q <- density(gpt, from = min(x_grid),
               to = max(x_grid), n = 2048)

  # Avoid zero densities
  eps <- 1e-12

  p_values <- approx(p$x, p$y, xout = x_grid)$y + eps
  q_values <- approx(q$x, q$y, xout = x_grid)$y + eps

  # Normalize
  p_values <- p_values / sum(p_values)
  q_values <- q_values / sum(q_values)

  # KL divergence
  sum(p_values * log(p_values / q_values))
}

KL_results <- gpt_data %>%
  distinct(participant, Itemtype) %>%
  group_by(participant, Itemtype) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    current_model <- .y$participant
    current_itemtype <- .y$Itemtype

    human_values <- human_data %>%
      filter(Itemtype == current_itemtype) %>%
      pull(cloze_probability)

    gpt_values <- gpt_data %>%
      filter(
        participant == current_model,
        Itemtype == current_itemtype
      ) %>%
      pull(cloze_probability)

    tibble(
      KL_divergence = calculate_KL(
        human_values,
        gpt_values
      )
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

print(KL_results)

# plot
ggplot(KL_results, 
       aes(x = participant, 
           y = KL_divergence, 
           fill = Itemtype)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "GPT model",
    y = "KL divergence",
    fill = "Itemtype"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
```

## LME model

### prepare the data and check fixed effects

```{r}
# transfer to factor and set the baseline
highest_cloze_all <- highest_cloze_all %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    participant = relevel(as.factor(participant), ref = "human"),
    Itemtype = relevel(as.factor(Itemtype), ref = "English"))

# check whether there are fixed effects
# for comparison, we need to set REML = FALSE because different fixed effect can not be compared with TRUE

# null model
m0 <- lmer(cloze_probability ~ 1 + (1 | inner_number), data = highest_cloze_all, REML = FALSE)

# participant
m1 <- lmer(cloze_probability ~ participant + (1 | inner_number), data = highest_cloze_all, REML = FALSE)
anova(m0, m1) # check whether participant has effect -> Yes, there is a participant effect

# + Itemtype
m2 <- lmer(cloze_probability ~ participant + Itemtype + (1 | inner_number), data = highest_cloze_all, REML = FALSE)
anova(m1, m2)

# interaction (participant * Itemtype)
m3 <- lmer(cloze_probability ~ participant * Itemtype + (1 | inner_number), data = highest_cloze_all, REML = FALSE)
anova(m2, m3)
```

The anova results show that there are significant participant and Itemtype effets, and the interaction effect of participant and Itemtype.

### final LME model

```{r}
# in the final model, we change REML = TRUE
model <- lmer(cloze_probability ~ participant * Itemtype + (1 | inner_number), data = highest_cloze_all, REML = TRUE)
summary(model)
```

Participant effect: The highest cloze probability of human under English condition is 0.74, all LLMs have higher cloze probability than human (Claude = 0.26, GPT = 0.22, Mistral = 0.24), indicating that participant has significant effects and LLMs achieve higher cloze probability than human under English condition.

Itemtype effect: Humans are not sensitive to Itemtype (-0.009740).

Interaction effect: compare to human, Claude and Mistral are not affected by the Itemtype, while GPT achieves lower cloze probability under code-switching condition (GPT + English = 0.741 + 0.22 = 0.963, GPT + code-switching = 0.963 - 0.0097 - 0.0665 ≈ 0.887).
